_meta.why: Slow-moving data does not go wrong loudly. A scraper that breaks throws an error and pages somebody; a championship that finished in November and never got its row just sits there looking finished, and the board quietly answers a question about 2026 with 2024's facts. Every entry below is a dataset nobody will notice going stale, paired with the date it becomes stale. scripts/check-data-currency.mjs reads this and says what the site currently owes.
_meta.howToAddOne: Annual events need the date their season ends and a probe the checker already implements. Rankings need the file and how old their asOf may get. If you add a data source that updates less often than weekly and has no scheduled job behind it, it belongs here, and adding it costs one object.
_meta.grace: graceDays is how long after the event a missing row is merely late rather than wrong. It is generous on purpose: results are often not final on the day, and a gate that shouts the morning after a race gets ignored within a month.

annual.label: FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup
annual.why: Quadrennial, so everyYears keeps a non-World-Cup year from demanding a row. The 2026 edition (Germany) is on the clock from 15 September 2026, which is when .github/workflows/wwc-2026-tracker.yml should have found a final; a missing row after that is the tracker having failed quietly.

snapshots.label: FHFA house price index (/business/economy/housing)
snapshots.why: FHFA publishes quarterly, about two months after quarter end; the mini's economy-housing job rebuilds weekly, so a build older than four months means the job stopped.

snapshots.label: IIHF men's world ranking
snapshots.why: IIHF republishes after each Worlds, so roughly annual.

snapshots.label: FIVB senior world ranking
snapshots.why: FIVB restates after each major event, several times a year.

snapshots.label: Handball world ranking
snapshots.why: handballranking.com moves after each major tournament.

snapshots.label: FIFA women's world ranking
snapshots.why: FIFA publishes quarterly, so anything older than two cycles is stale.

snapshots.label: ZZC ranking-only feed
snapshots.why: Hand-maintained. The whole point of the limit is that nothing else will remind anyone.

snapshots.label: Against Expectation, five continental leagues
snapshots.why: engsoccerdata ships one batch a season, so the ledger for Spain, Italy, Germany, France and the Netherlands is only as current as the last annual pull into data/football/esd/.

snapshots.label: Club squad market value, six leagues
snapshots.why: Transfermarkt reprices in waves each December and June with continuous revaluation between, so a corpus more than four months old is missing a repricing. The upstream transfermarkt-datasets pipeline has been paused since July 2026; when this goes overdue that is the reason to check.

snapshots.label: UN World Population Prospects (country hubs, /countries/2100)
snapshots.why: The UN revises WPP every two years (July 2024, next expected mid-2026); scripts/countries/build_population_2100.py is run by hand from the CSVs downloaded on the Windows box, so an index older than thirty months means a revision was missed.

snapshots.label: The Money Ledger: transfer fees per club and season, six leagues
snapshots.why: Same corpus as club-value (Transfermarkt via transfermarkt-datasets, paused since July 2026); asOf is the source's last transfer date. Rebuild with scripts/football/build_transfer_ledger.py --write after re-downloading transfers.csv.gz whenever the value corpus is refreshed, so the two never disagree on a month.

snapshots.label: Organisation memberships (/orgs, country pages, the 2100 blocs)
snapshots.why: asOf is the date every membership was last verified by hand against the organisations' own records (2026-09-10 the first time; the UAE had left OPEC four months earlier and the site still listed it). The monthly Wikidata tripwire (orgs-monthly.yml) catches additions between verifications; this gate says when the hand check itself is overdue.
